intro: “Was” and “were” are the past of “to be”. Use them to say where you were, how you felt, what the weather was like or how an event was. It is your first step to talk about the past, before other verbs (lessons 41 and 42).
objectifs: Use “to be” in the past: I was, you were, he was, we were, they were.
Make negatives (wasn't, weren't), questions and short answers.
Use past time expressions: yesterday, last week, two days ago.
Say when and where you were born (I was born…) and use there was / there were.

texte: In the past, “to be” has only two forms: “was” with I, he, she, it, and “were” with you, we, they.
The past of “to be” describes a past state (I was tired) and a past fact (I was in Paris last week).
sections.note: Use “you were” for one person and for many people. “You was” is wrong in standard English.

texte: Negative: add “not”: was not → wasn't, were not → weren't. Never use “did” with “to be”.
Question: put the verb before the subject: “Were you at work?”, “Was the film good?”. With a question word: “Where were you?”, “Why was she late?”
Short answers: “Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.”, “Yes, they were. / No, they weren't.”

lignes: Yes, they were. / No, they weren't.
How was your weekend? — It was great!

exemples: Was the exam difficult? — No, it wasn't.
Why were you late? — Because the bus was late.

texte: Like in the present, “was / were” is for place, state, feelings, age, weather and description: “I was 18 in 2010”, “The hotel was very nice”.
“How was…?” is the perfect question to ask someone's opinion about a past event: “How was the party?”, “How was your trip?”.
In the past, “there is / there are” becomes “there was / there were”: “There was a problem.”, “There were a lot of people.”
exemples: There were twenty people at the party.
How was your trip to Kribi? — It was wonderful, but the road was long.

texte: In English, we always talk about birth in the past: “I was born in 1995”, “She was born in Bafoussam”. “I am born” is wrong.
Prepositions: “in” + year, month or place (I was born in May / in Liège); “on” + exact date (I was born on the 3rd of March).
exemples: Where were you born? — I was born in Quebec City.
My son was born on the 12th of June 2020.

texte: “yesterday”, “yesterday morning / afternoon / evening”, “last night”, “last week / month / year / Monday”, “in 2015”, “when I was a child”.
“Ago” goes AFTER the period of time: “two days ago”, “ten years ago”. Use no preposition or article before “last” and “yesterday”: “last week”, not “the last week” or “in last week”.

lignes: the week / year before this one

exemples: I was in Montreal three years ago.
When I was a child, I was very shy.

formule: I / he / she / it was · you / we / they were · wasn't / weren't · Was…? Were…? · I was born in…
prononciation: In positive sentences, “was” and “were” are weak: “I was tired” = /aɪ wəz ˈtaɪəd/; “we were late” = /wi wə ˈleɪt/.
In short answers and when you stress them, they are strong: “Yes, I WAS” /wɒz/, “Yes, they WERE” /wɜː/.
“wasn't” /ˈwɒznt/ and “weren't” /wɜːnt/: the final t is light, but you hear the n clearly.
Don't confuse “were” /wɜː/ and “where” /weə/: “Where were you?” = /ˈweə wə ju/.
“born” /bɔːn/: a long vowel; in British English you don't say the r.
erreurs: We always talk about birth in the past.
I was tired the last week.
I was in Paris before two years.
I was in Paris two years ago.
There were a lot of people.

dialogue.contexte: Monday morning in an office in Douala. Joël asks his colleague Rose about her weekend.
lignes: Good morning, Rose! How was your weekend?
It was great, thanks! I was in Limbe with my family.
Lucky you! Was the weather good?
Yes, it was sunny and the beach was beautiful. But there were a lot of people.
Oh yes, they were very happy. And you? Where were you on Saturday? You weren't at the football match.
No, I wasn't. I was at home. I was ill.
Oh no! Are you OK now?

mots: I was at the doctor's yesterday.
We were in Ghent last month.
She was here ten minutes ago.

exercices.consigne: Write the sentence in the negative (short form).
Write the question and the short answer.
items: Were you at home last night? — Yes, I was.
Was the hotel expensive? — No, it wasn't.
Were your friends at the party? — Yes, they were.
Was Paul in the office yesterday? — No, he wasn't.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: Before two days, it was very cold.
Two days ago, it was very cold.
There was a lot of people at the market.
There were a lot of people at the market.

exercices.consigne: Write about your last weekend in four or five sentences with was, were, wasn't, weren't and there was / there were.
items: Last weekend I was in Brussels with my sister. The weather wasn't very good: it was cloudy and cold. On Saturday we were at a concert. There were a lot of people and the music was fantastic. We were very tired on Sunday!

a_retenir: was with I, he, she, it; were with you, we, they.
Negative: wasn't / weren't; question: Was she…? Were you…?; never “did” with “be”.
How was your weekend? — It was great!; there was / there were.
Birth in the past: I was born in 1995 / on the 3rd of March.
yesterday, last week (no article), two days ago (ago after the period).
